text: Picture Earth from above the north pole, with the sea drawn larger than it is.
The Moon's pull lifts the water on the near side into a bulge, toward the Moon.
Earth is pulled away from the water on the far side, so a second bulge forms there too.
As Earth turns under these two bulges, each coast passes through one high tide and one low tide.
Because the Moon moves on, a full tide cycle takes about twelve hours and twenty-five minutes.
